title: Israel's days, your way
hookLine: Jews mark Israel's memorial and independence days in many ways, or not at all
tomorrow: why would anyone stay up all night on purpose?

cards: Some holidays are easy at a family dinner. Others come with a pause, a look across the table, and somebody changing the subject.
For some Jewish families, Israel's two spring days are like that: Yom HaZikaron, a memorial day for fallen soldiers and victims of terror, and right after it, Yom HaAtzmaut, Independence Day.
So how do you mark a day your family argues about? The tradition has two lines for this, and both are older than the argument.

teach.h: MANY WAYS, OR NOT AT ALL.
teach.b: Jews mark these days in many ways, or not at all. Some stand still for a memorial siren or light a candle on the first day, then celebrate on the second. Some keep the first and not the second.
Some keep neither, for reasons of faith or conscience. There's no single script, but there are two lines.

teach.h: PRAY FOR THE PEACE OF JERUSALEM.
teach.b: A Psalm: "Pray for the peace of Jerusalem; may they prosper that love thee."

And Hillel, in Pirkei Avot: do not judge your fellow until you have reached their place. Between those two lines there's room for your own way, chosen honestly, and room for the uncle who chose differently.
Now the week, back in one breath. The cleaning: dust is not chametz. The seder: you can lead it.
Its old script: add your question. Matzah: bread of freedom. The Omer: a trait a week.
Yom HaShoah: one name. From a kitchen at midnight to a single candle, a week of the year, lived.

how: Jews mark Yom HaZikaron and Yom HaAtzmaut in many ways: some stand for a memorial siren, light candles or attend ceremonies and then celebrate; some keep only the memorial day; some do not mark them, for religious or personal reasons.

games.q: your cousin lights a candle on the memorial day but skips the celebration the next day. a friend calls that half-hearted. what does Hillel's line suggest?
o: don't judge until you reach their place; ask what it means to them.
your friend has a point; it should be both days or neither.
say nothing about it, since these aren't real Jewish days anyway.
games.why: the tradition gives no single script for these days. Hillel's line leaves room for a choice made honestly, including one different from yours.

practice: Close your eyes and bring to mind one person in your family, or a friend, who sees these days differently than you do. Hold their face for a few breaths without arguing back, only seeing where they're standing.
Then let the picture go and open your eyes.

carryVoice: A line to keep: your own way, chosen honestly, with room at the table for someone else's. Next week opens with a long night.
